prompt.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: a FIVE-FRAME SPRITE SHEET of a Song dynasty young mother walking with her baby tied on her back: one standing pose plus one complete four-frame walk cycle, walking toward the RIGHT of the image. TWO reference images. The FIRST shows the exact character(s) to draw: copy identity, face, hair, clothing colours and carried objects from it. Its camera angle may be from behind or from above; IGNORE that angle. The SECOND reference is a finished walk sheet of a different person: copy ONLY its camera angle (eye-level three-quarter side view, the same as every other figure on the street), its figure scale and its five-cell layout. Do NOT copy that person. Keep: black hair bun, lavender-grey jacket, cream long skirt, dark cloth shoes, the SAME baby in a blue floral carrying cloth on her back with rust-orange ties crossing her chest, the baby's head peeking over her left shoulder. Her right hand holds the cloth tie at her chest, her left arm swings gently. The baby stays snugly in the same place in every cell and only bobs with her steps. Cell 1 = standing at rest, facing right. Cell 2 = contact: front leg forward with heel touching the ground, back leg on its toes, longest stride. Cell 3 = passing: weight on the straight supporting leg under the body, the other leg bent and passing forward, foot just off the ground. Cell 4 = contact with the opposite leg forward, mirror of cell 2. Cell 5 = passing with the opposite leg, mirror of cell 3. The head stays at the same height and the same horizontal position in every walking cell; the body only bobs very slightly. Correct leg anatomy, robe and skirt hems swing with the legs, no extra limbs. Fine ink outlines and muted antique Chinese watercolor exactly matching the first reference, same line weight, same palette, same paper-grain shading. Truly transparent alpha background, no ground shadow, no glow, no grid lines, no numbers, no text. One single horizontal row of 5 equal-width cells, all walking toward the RIGHT of the image, centered in each cell with generous margin so heads, tools, sheaves, umbrellas and feet never touch a cell edge. Identical figure size and identical camera angle in every cell. Make every cell match each other as strictly as possible.
